topIssues.title: kona-node: prevent delegated finalized-head regression
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
A stale delegated source can make Kona request a backward finalized-head update. This is the finalized-monotonicity scope of the delegated derivation parity tracker.

## Reproduction

With local unsafe=30, safe=20, finalized=10, a delegate reports an existing finalized block 5. FinalizeTask checks only that the target is no higher than safe, sends an FCU with finalized=5, and records finalized=5 if EL returns VALID.

The actual Kona engine unit test proves the backward request and acceptance logic. It does **not** establish that real op-reth accepts a finalized regression. EL rejection could instead cause recovery errors.

Compare [Kona finalization](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/49efa52bcb3ecaeea390d333de63b37b8650aa75/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/task_queue/tasks/finalize/task.rs#L32-L75) with [op-node's external finalized monotonicity guard](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/4f0f0eaf92b923f61d11a9405b88880999399529/op-node/rollup/engine/engine_controller.go#L1535-L1538).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Older finalized references do not emit backward FCUs or regress CL finalized state.
- [ ] Repeated identical finalized references remain harmless while allowing legitimate pending EL synchronization.
- [ ] Conflicting hashes at the current finalized height are rejected safely rather than silently replacing finality.
- [ ] Preserve hash-pinned lookup, height validation, and safe/finalized ordering checks.
- [ ] Cover older, identical, conflicting-same-height, and legitimate advancing targets.
- [ ] Keep the implementation independent of catch-up liveness and forkchoice delivery/retry fixes.

Confirmed on deployed `49efa52` and PR #23627 tip `2763f5e`; relevant code is unchanged on develop `cfec650e57`. Implement as an independent PR against develop.

Parent tracker: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/545 (target November 5, 2026).

topIssues.title: kona-node: verify delegated derivation parity against op-node
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
Part of ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#545.

The tracker's completion criteria include verification work that no fix PR covers. This issue tracks it so the parity claim rests on exercised behavior, not only on unit tests in the three core fixes (#23675, #23676, #23677).

Scope:
- Verify safe and finalized progress by block hash and ancestry, comparing CL and EL labels, with unsafe production paused.
- Exercise source-ahead catch-up and an EL answering SYNCING followed by VALID, including unchanged-target retries and eventual recovery.
- Exercise stale-source finalized references and confirm finalized never moves backward and conflicting hashes are not accepted.
- Run the follow-source acceptance cases against Kona, or explicitly retain and link the remaining gaps: #22272, #22273, #22274.
- Record results on #545 and tick the corresponding completion checkboxes.

topIssues.title: flaky test: `TestInteropFaultProofs_InvalidBlock`
topIssues.author: maurelian
topIssues.body:
https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/139419/workflows/feb351e1-7e49-410d-a1ee-27a572f0e50e/jobs/5877424

Job `memory-all-opn-op-reth-fusaka`, merge-queue run for ethereum-optimism/optimism#23771 (contracts-only change), 2026-11-10.

```
Error Trace: op-devstack/dsl/eoa.go:392
             op-acceptance-tests/tests/superfaultproofs/superfaultproofs.go:1196
             op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/proofs/serial/interop_fault_proofs_test.go:81
Error:       Received unexpected error:
             operation failed permanently after 5 attempts: not found
Messages:    invalid exec msg receipt not found
```

About 10s before the assertion, chain 902 reorged out the unsafe block (13) that carried the invalid exec message tx:

```
WARN L2 reorg: existing unsafe block does not match derived attributes from L1 component=supernode chain_id=902
  err="transaction 0 does not match ..." unsafe=ce53f5..f22801:13 pending_safe=ac50d9..a4c010:12
```

The mismatch is in the L1 info deposit (different L1 origin), so the tx is dropped and its receipt is never found. Looks like a race between sequencing and L1 derivation rather than a code regression. CircleCI insights also shows a failure in `memory-all-kona-op-reth-fusaka` (1/100 runs on develop).

topIssues.title: opgeth-decoupling: migrate tests (op-e2e L2 call sites, wait.go split, delete op-e2e/opgeth, audit op-devstack/sysgo)
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #20257. See plan §12, §13 in the op-geth decoupling doc (PR #19767).

## Goal

Migrate the integration/acceptance test layer to work with upstream go-ethereum. `op-acceptance-tests` is already half-decoupled (uses `op-devstack` DSL, zero direct `ethclient` imports) — improvements to `apis.EthClient` ripple through automatically. Main work is in `op-e2e` and `op-devstack/sysgo`.

## Scope

### `op-e2e/e2eutils/geth/wait.go` — split into header-only + full-block variants

These helpers use only standard go-ethereum APIs (no OP-Stack specifics), but `WaitForBlock` / `WaitForBlockToBeSafe` / `WaitForBlockToBeFinalized` transitively call `BlockByNumber`, which fails on L2 due to deposit-tx decoding.

Most callers discard the returned `*types.Block` (`_, err := geth.WaitForBlock(...)`). Plan:
- Add `WaitForBlockHeight(num, client)` returning `*types.Header` via `HeaderByNumber` — L2-safe even under upstream.
- Keep `WaitForBlock` for the few callers that read block body fields; migrate it to an `apis.EthClient`-backed impl.
- `WaitForTransaction` return type → `*optypes.Receipt` (ripples from #20264).
- `WaitUntilTransactionNotFound`: callers use non-deposit user txs; document and keep, migrate if needed.

### Direct L2 block/tx call sites in op-e2e (19 sites, 9 files)

Migrate to `apis.EthClient` or header-only variant:
- `op-e2e/actions/proofs/isthmus_fork_test.go` (3 sites)
- `op-e2e/actions/upgrades/ecotone_fork_test.go` (3 sites)
- `op-e2e/actions/helpers/user.go` (2 sites, `CrossLayerUser`)
- `op-e2e/faultproofs/cannon_benchmark_test.go` (1 site)
- `op-e2e/interop/interop_test.go` (1 site, `BlockByHash`)
- `op-e2e/system/bridge/validity_test.go` (1 site)
- `op-e2e/system/conductor/system_adminrpc_test.go` (3 sites)
- `op-e2e/system/fees/*.go` (3 sites)
- `op-e2e/system/verifier/legacy_pending_test.go` (2 sites)

### `op-e2e/system/e2esys.SystemConfig.L2Client`

Change from `*ethclient.Client` to `apis.EthClient`.

### `op-devstack/sysgo/` audit

Direct `ethclient.Dial` / `ethclient.NewClient` calls in ~7 files (mostly L1 contract deployment / faultproof game setup). Per-file audit: L1 callers stay on `*ethclient.Client` (safe); any L2 callers migrate to `op-service/sources.EthClient`.

### Delete `op-e2e/opgeth/`

This package exercises op-geth engine internals intentionally. Equivalent tests against op-reth will be introduced separately (tracked outside this issue). Delete the package as part of the decoupling.

## Dependencies

Blocked on: #20264 (`apis.EthClient` return-type changes and sources deposit-tx decoding).

topPRs.title: ci: pilot RWX with shared routing and shadow tests
topPRs.author: teddyknox
topPRs.body:
PR validation currently rebuilds op-reth in CircleCI and lacks executed RWX parity evidence. This pilot runs the complete op-reth release producer and its three associated checks alongside shared routing, Go lint/Rust formatting, Go rollup tests and four standard-contract configurations. CircleCI continues to own the required gates.

The op-reth shadow builds both release binaries, runs every selected `reth-optimism-node` test through a nextest archive, generates fresh compact vectors with pinned develop and reads them with the PR binary, and regenerates both superchain snapshots. It uses shared dependency downloads, content caching, separate native tool caches for Cargo targets and sccache, parallel codec compilers, pinned tools and SHA-bound artifacts. Checksum-matching superchain bundles retain their timestamps. Release, integration and codec consumers mount artifacts directly instead of inheriting compiler-cache layers. Every verdict and vector generation executes freshly.

Validation:

- At `0b7935e7339726c1b1166be6372fbf057fb251dd`, [native op-reth CI](https://cloud.rwx.com/optimism/runs/0d4989f8fc044b48888ba7cdda9e9b2a) passed all four workloads in **6m20s**. All 50 runnable integration cases passed; one explicitly ignored case remained in discovery. Original JUnit identities and outcomes matched [CircleCI job 5625881](https://circleci.com/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/5625881) exactly. All four RWX status checks are green at this head.
- Direct artifact mounts removed both compiler-cache trees from the codec verifier. Its measured preparation fell from 171s at `99ccc76a` to 2s at this head, followed by fresh execution in 5s. The final consumer received a 622 MiB binary artifact and two small vector/provenance artifacts, and its metadata confirmed the PR checkout. Both observations are single samples, with different runner-local layer states.
- Before the bundle/artifact optimizations, the complete RWX run at `d2b90241` took 13m10s initially and [5m58s with warm tool caches](https://cloud.rwx.com/optimism/runs/2c7e09f8233541869ff6fa8771b3d372). A [forced target-cache probe](https://cloud.rwx.com/optimism/runs/8545eb684d094e13abc4e91fdab645fe) after bundle retention executed snapshot preparation in 7s, with six Rust sccache hits and zero misses; fresh regeneration still ran for 24s.
- An [empty-target probe](https://cloud.rwx.com/optimism/runs/8552f40db3314cf282583313806e0be6) produced 263 Rust hits and zero misses in 36s. An [identical-input release rerun](https://cloud.rwx.com/optimism/runs/be0b0006cd5044c88739ec46cd81f2d6) reused the compiler content cache and finished the release path in 8s, including fresh binary verification. A separate warm release rebuild recorded 27 Rust hits and no misses but still spent 236s compiling/linking; content reuse and incremental reuse have different benefits.
- An [intentional CLI-only test fault](https://cloud.rwx.com/optimism/runs/add6576e7432497a8a1e3f85a40a8313) failed the task and run, preserved nextest's exit 100, and retained original JUnit and partial coverage. Committed Rust tests were unchanged.
- 22 cache/provenance/report regression tests, 35 routing scenarios, shell checks and RWX configuration validation passed. The final native artifact consumers inherited no op-reth compiler caches; only snapshot regeneration retained Cargo targets.

Implementation coverage is **10/86 expanded PR jobs, about 12%**. The [parity checklist](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/codex/rwx-ci-pilot/docs/ai/rwx-parity-todos.md) and [measurements](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/codex/rwx-ci-pilot/docs/ai/rwx-migration.md#first-hosted-measurements) track representative Rust source-change probes, repeated actual-resource timings and billed usage, smaller tool/compiler layers, and a protected cache-rebuild policy before promotion. Whole-run duration, compiler phases and billed cost remain separate measurements; declared resource classes do not prove identical hardware. Full Go/acceptance producers and consumers, remaining Rust/contracts, routing and identity cutover remain open.

Earlier Go/contract comparisons at `587b4c3a` still need authoritative CircleCI discovery, 178 contract skip reasons and fresh evidence for 17 cached Go cases. Schedules, publishing and privileged writer ownership remain with CircleCI. The cache-only RWX vault has no production credentials and restricted pilot/develop writers; remove the temporary pilot grant and evict pilot cache entries before promotion.

This single draft PR replaces #23141, #23142, #23144 and #23148 and remains the ongoing home for the pilot.

topPRs.title: Add Lean proof of the super-aggregation coverage checks
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
Adds a Lean proof that `SuperAggregationInputs::validate` only accepts aggregations whose child outputs form one contiguous chain of super roots from the starting root to the root claim, with one range-derived block per chain and one consolidation step at every timestamp in between.

The Rust is extracted with Charon and Aeneas into `rust/kona/sp1/verification`. The main theorem is `KonaSp1.aggregation_sound`. It assumes child-proof soundness and `l2_sequence_number < u64::MAX`; the README lists the full trust base. `#print axioms` shows only Lean's standard axioms and the opaque super-root hash.

The `super_root.rs` change is only to suit the extractor: loops that returned early from nested or post-`?` positions move into private helpers, with the same accepted inputs and error order. A new test covers a chain-ID mismatch in a later timestamp block, the one loop that was rewritten rather than moved.

CI does not build the Lean project yet. `scripts/extract.sh` regenerates the generated files and `lake build` checks the proofs.

topPRs.title: op-deployer,op-chain-ops!: run every deploy script on forge and delete the Go script host
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
This PR is split into a stack for review: #23663 → #23664 → #23665 → #23666 → #23667 → #23668 → #23669. The stack has later review fixes; this PR stays open as the CI-green reference.

op-deployer ran its deploy scripts on `op-chain-ops/script`, an in-process Go EVM. That host needs EVM hooks that only op-geth has (cheatcode precompiles, pranks, no code-size limit), so it blocks the move to upstream go-ethereum (#20266). After this PR, forge is the only script engine, and the Go host and `op-chain-ops/interopgen` are deleted.

**Effect on users**

- op-deployer runs forge for every deployment, and anvil for `prepare` and `continue`. It downloads the pinned Foundry release on Linux and macOS when the tools are not on PATH. The Docker images ship both.
- Genesis deployments (`apply --deployment-target genesis`, op-e2e, sysgo) run the scripts offline on forge. The L1 and L2 genesis output does not change: before the switch, a differential test found equal state roots from both engines on eight reference intents.
- Live `apply` and `bootstrap` broadcast with forge, one transaction at a time, and no longer through op-service's txmgr. As txmgr did, each transaction gets the node's gas estimate just before forge sends it, a tip of at least 1 gwei, and a fee cap of twice the base fee (at least 1 gwei) plus the tip. Unlike txmgr, forge does not bump the fee of, or resubmit, a stuck transaction. forge gets the deployer key in a temporary encrypted keystore that only the user can read, never on its command line.
- `prepare` and `continue` simulate the deployment on an ephemeral anvil fork of the L1, as the deployer, without its key. `continue` then checks the simulated transactions and replays them to L1 through txmgr.
- op-deployer never compiles. It refuses a contracts bundle that would make forge compile, or whose scripts have no `runWithBytes` entrypoint, and it stops forge as soon as forge starts to compile. So a bundle must come from the contracts release of the same op-deployer release: an `https://` or `file://` bundle of an earlier release is refused (`tag://` locators were already rejected). The default, `embedded`, works.
- A contracts bundle is a forge project, so op-deployer does not trust its `foundry.toml`: scripts run without the FFI cheatcode, with file access only to the artifacts and to op-deployer's state directory, and forge scripts and anvil inherit only the environment variables that they need (`verify-contract` keeps the full environment, for its API key). anvil listens on loopback without CORS.
- forge runs need the `lib/` sources of the bundle but no solc compiler. Each forge script loads every artifact of the project, about 1.3 GB, so forge runs take one of `GOMAXPROCS/2` slots per host.
- forge's output goes to stderr. A failed script reports its revert reason.
- Removed: the `calldata` and `noop` deployment targets, `op-deployer manage`, the `--use-forge` and `--forge-slow-broadcast` flags, the Windows release binaries and `DeploymentCalldata` in `state.json`. contracts-bedrock loses the `InteropMigration` script and `DummyCaller`.

**Reasons the diff does not show**

- Every forge run uses its own copy of the compile cache and its own broadcast directory, so that concurrent runs (devstack) do not interfere.
- Each broadcast sends one transaction at a time. Without `--slow`, forge waited forever when a node dropped one of several transactions that it sent at once.
- Bundle builds run one `forge script` to warm the script cache, as CI's `forge-build` already does. A single script's compile can choose other solc versions than the project build, and then forge compiles on the first run. The builds then check that a second run compiles nothing, and fail if it does.
- The interop harness and sysgo now run the interop migration on a live L1 through an EIP-7702 delegation from the ProxyAdmin owner, not in the genesis state. The L1 activates Prague at genesis for this.
- The test `RetryProxy` (op-service) now gives a client error (4xx, but not 429) to the client at once. forge calls methods such as `anvil_nodeInfo` that a proxyd endpoint answers with 403, and the proxy held each of these calls for about 40 s of retries, so the Sepolia tests of `init` timed out.
- sysgo waits for the L1 transaction index before it deploys: geth rejects receipt queries until its first indexing pass is done, and forge stops after a few quick retries.
- #23309 (genesis-output changes) is not in this PR, on purpose. It changes genesis output, which this PR must not do.
- CI jobs that run op-deployer from the checkout (op-e2e, sysgo, kona proof tests) now check out the contracts `lib/` submodules: forge reads the sources to check its compile cache, where the Go host read only artifact JSON.
- forge runs are not `--offline`: offline, forge requires every solc version of the cache installed even when it compiles nothing. Online, it resolves them from its built-in list and runs the cached artifacts.
- The `forge` package tests (anvil fork, compile stop, sandbox, environment, slots) run in CI only after #23643, which removes the package from the CI exclusion list.

**Review findings not fixed here**

- Live `apply`/`bootstrap` could keep txmgr by simulating on an anvil fork and replaying, as `continue` does. The #23300 plan chose `forge script --broadcast` for live deploys; this is a follow-up if fee bumping matters for these one-time deployments.
- The op-e2e interop harness and sysgo could share one `opcm.MigrateInput` type, and sysgo could check that its rollup configs and dependency set name the same chains, as interopgen did. Both are follow-ups.
- `opcm.NewForgeClient` takes no context for the forge download, and `opcm.PermissionedGameStartingAnchorRoot` now has only test users. Both are unchanged.
- Security review, not fixed: `continue` checks the sender, target, type and value of the call it replays, but not its calldata against the prepared input (that needs the script's encoding in Go); the RPC URL stays on the command line of forge and anvil, which have no environment binding for it; a crash during a broadcast can leave the encrypted keystore and its password file in a directory that only the user can read (forge refuses a password pipe); and a forge binary in the cache directory is trusted by its version.

Closes #23300, #23301, #23302, #23304, #23305, #23306, #23307 and #23308.

BREAKING CHANGE: The Go packages `op-chain-ops/script`, `op-chain-ops/interopgen`, `op-deployer/pkg/env`, `op-deployer/pkg/deployer/manage` and `op-deployer/pkg/deployer/upgrade` are removed. So are `opcm.Scripts`, the script-host `opcm` constructors, the `opcm.*ViaForge` functions (now `opcm.DeploySuperchain`, `opcm.DeployImplementations`, `opcm.DeployOPChain`, `opcm.DeployAltDA`, `opcm.DeployDisputeGame`, `opcm.DeployMIPS`, `opcm.DeployAlphabetVM`, `opcm.ReadImplementationAddresses` and `opcm.ReadSuperchainDeployment`, which take an `opcm.ForgeEnv`), `ApplyPipelineOpts.PrivateKey`, `UseForge` and `ReceiptQueryInterval`, and in `broadcaster` the `Broadcaster` interface, `CalldataBroadcaster`, `CaptureBroadcaster`, `NoopBroadcaster` and `BroadcastCreate2`. Go programs run Solidity scripts with forge, for example through op-deployer's `forge` package, take the upgrade input types from `opcm`, and build interop test worlds with an op-deployer intent. op-deployer users get forge and anvil from the release images, or let op-deployer download them. Users of `--use-forge`, `--forge-slow-broadcast`, or the `calldata` and `noop` targets drop them; forge is always used.
